newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called 50 cts to $1 down, Brent steady.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called 50 cts to $1 down, Brent steady.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were called to open 50 cents to $1.00 down on Tuesday while brokers expected Brent crude to open unchanged to five cents weaker.
June gas oil closed $1.50 up $174 a tonne on Tuesday and July Brent ended 12 cents up at $19.52, 10 cents off the session high having failed to break through resistance, brokers said.
"We were looking for a stronger close last night but we didn't get it," said one.
Some brokers said the failure of NYMEX crude to close above $21.00 lent weakness to the market.
But others saw some technical strength left in the market.
"This market has been a step ahead of the fundamentals for a couple of weeks now and technically it may want to break to the upside," a broker said.
But fundamental news was seen bearish, with reports that the United States has decided to support a rollover of the United Nations oil-for-food deal with Iraq.
Apparent lack of enthusiasm by the U.S. for a renewal of the deal was seen as the main stumbling block to an agreement.
"The U.S. has come out in support and that was the only thing holding it back," said one broker.
The U.N. Security Council is expected to adopt a resolution as early as Wednesday to extend the plan for another six months.
But brokers said that the market had already factored in the news with only big changes to export volumes likely to cause a sharp price movement.
